AeroMesh · single airfoil · 16 November 2026

A complete airfoil mesh, with the same boundary-layer quality at any camber

AeroMesh now produces a full structured mesh around a single airfoil, from the wall to the far field, exports it, and has been run in a flow solver. Across a 0–9% camber sweep the worst boundary-layer cell stays between 4.6° and 4.8° of skew. A mesh deformed to follow the same shapes reaches 48°.

What the mesher does now

The mesh is marched outward from the wall. Each layer is advanced by solving two equations: grid lines stay perpendicular to the layer below, and each cell gets a prescribed area. First cell height comes from Reynolds number and y⁺ (4.46 × 10⁻⁶ chord at Re = 6 million, y⁺ = 1).

The topology follows from the amended rule. Each trailing-edge corner asks for a number of elements equal to its fluid angle divided by 90°. A sharp edge (343°) asks for four, so one grid line must leave the body: the wake cut. A blunt edge is two corners of 262° asking for three each, so one line leaves from each corner and the base between them gets its own strip (magenta below). The code never asks which kind of edge it has; a sharp edge is the case where the strip has zero cells.

The claim, measured

For each section of a camber sweep, one mesh was regenerated from scratch and another was obtained by deforming a baseline mesh onto the new shape. The deformation is inverse-distance weighting with rotations, the algorithm used by mesh-movement packages, with the outer boundary held. Skew is the largest departure of a cell corner from 90°, taken over cells within 0.02 chord of the wall.

What this does and does not show

  • The remaining 4.6° is not a defect to tune away. A 343° corner split into four elements gives 85.9° each, so about 4° is the floor for this trailing edge, and it rises with the trailing-edge wedge angle (8.8° on a 24%-thick section).
  • Deformation keeps the first cell height and the wall-face orthogonality intact (y₁ within 0.2%, wall-face angle 1.9–2.1° at every camber). What it loses is the cell shape through the layer and around the trailing edge.
  • The fair competitor is not deformation but any generator re-run per shape. An O-grid marched the same way keeps y₁ too, but rounds the trailing edge: minimum angle about 50° against 85° here, and it predicted drag +3.6 counts away from the C-mesh on the same blunt section at 10°. pyHyp itself is not installed on this machine, so that comparison is against our own O-mesh.

Solver check: NACA 0012 at Re = 6 million

OpenFOAM 11, steady incompressible RANS, Spalart–Allmaras, wall-resolved. The reference is the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource case (CFL3D, 897 × 257 grid, Mach 0.15). The reference is compressible, so lift here is expected about 1% lower.

  • Drift is how far the 200-iteration mean of Cd moved from the previous 200 iterations; one count is 0.0001.
  • With the outer boundary at 50 chords drag at 10° comes out about 15 counts high. Moving it to 500 chords, as the reference does, removes that. Domain size, not the mesh near the wall, was the cause.
  • NASA describes these reference values as representative rather than exact, and other codes on the same page differ from CFL3D by a few counts.

Defects the outside referee found

OpenFOAM's checkMesh reported problems on meshes whose corner angles were all within 5° of square. Each came from neighbouring cells tapering at different rates, which moves a thin cell's centroid along its length. Our own metric now reproduces checkMesh's figure to three decimals and is asserted in the tests.

WhereReportedCauseAfter the fix
Far wake, first layers off the wake cut26 faces above 70°, worst 87.8°First cell height on the wake cut stopped growing 2 chords downstream, leaving cells 4 chords long and 0.0002 tall (aspect ratio 20,000).Cell height on the wake cut now grows with the streamwise spacing.
Inside the boundary layer over the leading edge35.2° at the tenth layerAveraging the along-wall cell size, meant for the far field, also changed the marched height of thin cells wherever wall spacing was graded.Averaging is weighted by cell aspect and leaves thin cells alone.
Across the wake line, blunt trailing edge35.4° between the C block and the base stripThe first cell on the wake cut and the strip beside it widened at different rates.Both use one widening law. Worst face in the mesh is now 12.9° at the default resolution and 3.7° on the fine mesh.
Around the trailing edge at very fine first cells45.7° at a first cell of 1e-6 chordStreamwise spacing at the trailing edge was a fixed number, so the corner cell's aspect ratio rose as the first cell shrank.Trailing-edge spacing is derived from the first cell height (aspect ratio 135).

Known limits

  • The outer boundary is wherever the march ends. It is not yet fitted to a supplied far-field curve, and it lands about 20% inside the nominal radius upstream because thick far-field cells fall short of their prescribed height.
  • The C block is identified as the longest wall segment between wake corners. That is right for one trailing edge and has not been tested on bodies with several reflex corners.
  • A corner-free body (ellipse, circle) gets the O-mesh; a single annulus around a body with a trailing edge is kept only as a baseline, since it rounds the corner at about 50°.
  • The blunt base face is not wall-resolved in its own normal direction: the first cell off the base is one trailing-edge spacing long, and y⁺ there reaches 25 while the rest of the wall averages below 2. The strip needs clustering towards the base.
  • The solver check is incompressible and uses one turbulence model on one section. Pressure and skin-friction distributions have not been compared, only forces.
  • The wake line leaves along the trailing-edge bisector and turns onto the x axis over one chord. The mesher is not told the angle of attack.
  • First cell height is within 0.3% of the request on 12%-thick sections and within 1.1% on the 24%-thick one, at the trailing-edge corner node.
  • The earlier medial-axis blocking, the interpolated collar and the marched collar are untouched and are not used by this path.

What was added, and how to re-run it

  • src/aeromesh/mesh/: spacing.py (graded node distributions, first cell from y⁺), hyperbolic.py (the marcher), airfoil.py (o_mesh, c_mesh), structured.py (blocks and exact assembly checks), export.py (OpenFOAM, SU2, VTK).
  • src/aeromesh/quality/metrics.py: wall, boundary-layer and whole-mesh metrics, including the finite-volume non-orthogonality that matches checkMesh.
  • tests/test_airfoil_mesh.py: 21 tests, about 40 seconds.
  • examples/20_airfoil_mesh.py draws the figure above.
  • python validation/camber_sweep.py <work_dir> re-runs the sweep; run_naca0012.py then collect_naca0012.py re-run the solver cases (OpenFOAM 11 needed); make_report.py rebuilds this page from the results.
